title: Iterator Patterns
concept: Advanced iterator patterns — chain, zip, enumerate, flat_map, peekable — for complex data processing pipelines.
why: Real-world data processing needs more than map and filter. These advanced patterns solve common iteration challenges elegantly.
syntax_ref:
iter.chain(other_iter)     // Concatenate
iter.zip(other_iter)       // Pair elements
iter.enumerate()           // Add index
iter.flat_map(|x| inner)   // Flatten nested
iter.peekable()            // Look ahead
tips: chain is for sequential data, zip is for parallel data — know the difference
enumerate is cleaner than manual index tracking in a loop
flat_map turns one-to-many into one-to-one iteration
peekable lets you write parsers and state machines without consuming prematurely
common_mistakes: Using zip with iterators of unequal length — shorter one determines total length
Assuming chain modifies the original iterators — it just creates a new combined view
Using flat_map when a simpler solution (two loops) would be clearer
